newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Cars president says rebound strong.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Cars president says rebound strong.

text.p: The president of Volvo Cars, the car unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, said the car operation's rebound was much stronger than 1996 profits show, according to a Monday newspaper article.
"Sure, currencies played a part (in supporting earnings)," Volvo Cars' president Tuve Johannesson was quoted by domestic daily Svenska Dagbladet as saying.
"But we also had higher extra costs for research and development and for other investments in the industrial system which together totalled 870 million crowns.

"If you add costs of 400 million crowns for early retirements, it largely counterbalances currency gains. The underlying strength in the change is thereby stronger than what figures suggest," he told the newspaper.
Volvo Car's operating profit jumped 38 percent to 1.5 billion crowns in 1996 from a year earlier. Cost levels per car in the 850 and 900 series fell by 6,500 crowns last year.
Johannesson also said increased volumes on important markets, more efficient production and an increase proportion of expensive car sales boosted profits.
In an article in Sunday's edition of Svenska Dagbladet, the newspaper estimated that Volvo Cars should have a sustainable profitability of at least six billion crowns at year end.

"We can very well end up somewhere there, of course on condition that no dramatic changes will haappen which overturn our estimates," Johannesson told the newspaper, adding that this should not be seen as a forecast.
